clue.text: Skill fixing fence, if icy

indicators.note: fixing suggests putting right or rearranging, so the letters of the phrase before it are rebuilt

explanation.surface: A handyman's competence shown by repairing a fence despite the frost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fixing' reads as the job being done, but it signals rearranging FENCE IF ICY.
explanation.definitionFit: Skill in getting work done well and without waste is a near synonym.

clue.text: Branch of sweet chestnut's cut

indicators.note: a branch is a part off the main tree, so a part of these words is taken out of them

explanation.surface: A bough of a sweet chestnut tree has been lopped off.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters sit across the join of sweET CHestnut.
explanation.definitionFit: To cut lines into a metal plate or glass is the engraver's sense of the verb.

clue.text: Catch up after pro got left behind

indicators.note: after places the catch piece at the end of the answer

parts.note: pro means in favour of, for
taken as written

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: to catch fish is to net them

explanation.surface: A professional falls behind and has to catch up.
explanation.definitionFit: Something forgotten has been left out of mind, abandoned in memory.

clue.text: Charges people from the Highlands leading southern moves?

indicators.note: leading points to the letter at the front of the word for Highlanders as the one that travels
moves tells us that letter shifts from its place to somewhere else in the word

parts.note: Highlanders are Scots

explanation.surface: Scottish people take charge of a southern relocation and ask what it charges.
explanation.walkthrough: The first S of SCOTS travels to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Costs and charges are both the prices asked for something.

clue.text: Went in hospital department before daughter

parts.note: ENT is the ear, nose and throat department
ere is an old word for before

explanation.surface: Someone went into the hospital department ahead of their daughter.
explanation.definitionFit: Went in is a plain synonym of the past tense of enter.

clue.text: Company suggest leaving a place of learning

indicators.note: leaving says the letter a departs from the word for suggest

parts.note: to allege is to suggest or claim

explanation.surface: A firm proposes quitting an educational institution.
explanation.definitionFit: A college is an institution of higher education.

clue.text: Bound to leave

definitions.meaning: a bound is a jump, a little hop
to depart in a hurry, as in leaving town without paying

explanation.surface: Someone is obliged to go away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bound to' looks like 'obliged to', but Bound is one meaning on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: A light jump is one sense; departing suddenly, as from a meeting, is the other.

clue.text: Recognised kind of wine regularly taken out

indicators.note: taking out every other letter at a regular interval leaves the odd ones of the phrase

explanation.surface: A wine variety is acknowledged and served now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: K-i-N-d O-f W-i-N-e: keep the first, third, fifth letters and so on.
explanation.definitionFit: Recognised and known both describe something familiar or acknowledged.

clue.text: Putting on an act before start of theatrical finale

parts.note: pre is a prefix meaning before

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter

parts.note: a finale is an ending

explanation.surface: Someone performs ahead of a theatrical show's closing number.
explanation.definitionFit: Putting on an act is acting out a false show, feigning.

clue.text: Vehicles, vehicles — about time!

indicators.note: about means going round, so the word for vehicles surrounds the time letter

parts.note: cars are vehicles

explanation.surface: An exasperated cry that the vehicles have arrived at last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about time!' sounds like impatience, but 'about' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Carts are wheeled vehicles, often drawn by horses.

clue.text: Select Poe works to shorten

indicators.note: works as a verb means works over, reshapes, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An instruction to pick some of Poe's writings and cut them down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'works' looks like Poe's writings but is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To condense something by sliding sections into each other, as the instrument does, is to shorten it.

clue.text: What person in the Navy could want rubbish on board ship?

definitions.text: What person in the Navy could want

indicators.note: on board puts the rubbish inside the ship letters, as cargo is carried

parts.note: SS stands for steamship
tripe is nonsense, rubbish

explanation.surface: A sailor asks why they would want rubbish brought onto the vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: Stripes on a sleeve mark rank, so a sailor seeking promotion would want more of them.

clue.text: Old bishop and minister in study

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
to minister to someone is to serve them

explanation.surface: A retired bishop and a minister share a study.
explanation.walkthrough: 'minister' and 'study' look like nouns, a cleric and a room; both are verbs here.
explanation.definitionFit: To study something closely is to watch or examine it.

clue.text: Rushed for instance towards the West's diversity

parts.note: ran means rushed

indicators.note: in an across clue, west is leftward, so the letters read backwards

parts.note: EG abbreviates the Latin for for instance

explanation.surface: A tale of a hurried move west and the variety found there.
explanation.definitionFit: A wide range is a variety or spread of different things.

clue.text: Customs raid — it's not unusual

indicators.note: unusual says these letters appear in an unaccustomed order, rearranged

explanation.surface: A customs raid is protested as no rare event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Customs raid' looks like a border search, but Customs is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Customs are long-standing practices handed down, the same as inherited ways of doing things.

clue.text: Agitated conductor leading band's climax

indicators.note: leading puts the conductor in front of the following piece

parts.note: Sir Simon Rattle is a famous British orchestral conductor

indicators.note: a climax is the end, so the last letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: A conductor gets worked up as the band reaches its big finish.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone rattled is flustered and unsettled.

clue.text: Mad king wielding the whip

indicators.note: wielding means holding, so the king's name holds the word the

parts.note: King Lear goes mad in Shakespeare's play

explanation.surface: A deranged monarch brandishes a whip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'whip' looks like the thing wielded but is the verb defined.
explanation.definitionFit: To leather someone is to thrash them with a strap, so to beat or flog.

clue.text: Former lover suggested getting bare

parts.note: an ex is a former partner
to pose a question is to put it forward, suggest it

explanation.surface: An ex proposed stripping off.
explanation.definitionFit: Bare and laid open both describe something uncovered or unprotected.

clue.text: Some tailors initially longing to finish this?

definitions.text: Some tailors initially longing to finish this?

indicators.note: initially picks the opening letters of the words before it

parts.note: itching means longing, eager

explanation.surface: Tailors keen to complete a garment's needlework.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue describes the answer too: sewing is what a tailor wants to finish.
explanation.definitionFit: Needlework seams are what tailors must complete before a garment is done.

clue.text: Country retreat with distinguishing characteristic

parts.note: a den is a private hideaway
a mark is a distinctive trait

explanation.surface: Someone's hideaway has a feature that sets it apart.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scandinavian nation is a country.

clue.text: Thick stews in French cuisine, as they say in Paris

definitions.text: cuisine, as they say in Paris

indicators.note: stews as a verb means stirs and mixes up, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: the French for in is en

explanation.surface: Hearty French stews, described in the native phrase.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stews' looks like the food but is the anagram signal; the French word cuisine means the cooking room.
explanation.definitionFit: In French, cuisine is the word for the room where food is cooked.

clue.text: Hearing sounds back, son must be captivated

indicators.note: being captivated is being held captive, so the son letter is held inside
back means the word for sounds is read backwards

parts.note: noises are sounds

explanation.surface: A hearing reverberates, and a son is entranced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns NOISES to SESION, which then holds the extra S.
explanation.definitionFit: A court hearing is a sitting or session of the court.

clue.text: Head cleaner has mop bent over

indicators.note: bent means twisted out of shape, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: O is the cricket scoring abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: A cleaner in charge leans over a mop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head cleaner' reads as a senior cleaner but means hair wash.
explanation.definitionFit: The liquid used to wash one's hair cleans the head.

clue.text: Model of car and every train

parts.note: the Model T was Ford's famous early car
each means every

explanation.surface: A car model and every train are compared, like toy transport.
explanation.walkthrough: 'train' looks like the railway but is the verb, to instruct.
explanation.definitionFit: To train someone is to instruct them in a skill.

clue.text: Refusal to tuck into any bug

indicators.note: tucking into means slipping inside, so the refusal goes inside the word any

parts.note: no is a refusal

explanation.surface: Refusing to eat any insect at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tuck into' and 'bug' suggest eating insects; bug is the verb, to irritate.
explanation.definitionFit: To bug someone is to irritate or pester them.

clue.text: Business skill returned: very loudly in charge

indicators.note: returned means the word for skill comes back, written backwards

parts.note: art means skill
FF is the musical mark fortissimo, very loud

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper's knack has come back, and they run things noisily.
explanation.definitionFit: Traffic as trade or dealing, especially illicit buying and selling, is business.

clue.text: Female continually creating state of excitement

parts.note: ever means always, continually

explanation.surface: A woman keeps generating excitement.
explanation.definitionFit: A pitch of nervous excitement is figuratively a fever, as in fever pitch.

clue.text: Heroic exploit, whichever way you look at it

indicators.text: whichever way you look at it
indicators.note: reading the word forwards or backwards gives the same letters, so either direction works

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: A brave act that is heroic from every point of view.
explanation.definitionFit: A deed, as in doughty deeds, is a notable act or exploit.

clue.text: Keeping in power involved keeping quiet

indicators.note: keeping means holding, so the jumbled letters hold the quiet piece
involved means tangled up, so these letters are mixed

parts.note: sh is the call for quiet

explanation.surface: Holding on to power by staying discreet.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in someone's keeping means held in their possession, which is what holding title means.

clue.text: Say nothing in sin

indicators.note: in places the nothing letter inside the word for sin

parts.note: vice means sin, wickedness
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A command to stay silent about wrongdoing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Say' looks like a verb of speaking; it is the noun, a say in matters.
explanation.definitionFit: Having a say is having a voice, an opinion that counts.

clue.text: Holy man, the old thing that's painful to see around

definitions.text: thing that's painful to see around

parts.note: ST abbreviates saint
ye is an old form of the

explanation.surface: A saint, an old object hurting the eye.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to see around' means located round the organ of sight.
explanation.definitionFit: This inflamed swelling on the eyelid is sore, around the organ used for seeing.

clue.text: Fired up, 50% of encounters were angry

indicators.note: half of the ten-letter word, its first five letters, is used

parts.note: raged means were angry

explanation.surface: Half of all meetings ended in fury, getting people roused.
explanation.definitionFit: Being fired up is being emboldened and spurred on.
